summary: The prior report is a placeholder stub — domain "test", one item "r1" with evidence "e1" and gap "g1" — so it contains zero verified findings and its single "have" verdict is unsupported by any real file. The actual FSBO workflow is more built out than any stub could suggest: a registered daily cron (vercel.json:167-170) runs an Apify Zillow scrape, skip-traces owners, creates native crm_people leads, queues a CMA, emails Matt, and writes a fsbo_listings audit row; the operator surface lives at /admin/prospecting?kind=fsbo behind a real capability gate and a nav entry; the outbound intro SMS has a genuinely rigorous TCPA/suppression/idempotency pipeline. But there are three real defects: (1) nothing in the codebase ever sets fsbo_listings.status='gone', so the off-market compliance guard is permanently dead and sold/delisted FSBOs stay solicitable forever; (2) the cron's six sequential Apify run-sync calls at timeout=180 each can total 1080s against a 300s maxDuration, so later cities and the whole per-listing processing loop can be truncated mid-run; (3) an entire parallel FSBO dashboard stack (app/actions/fsbo-dashboard.ts, components/admin/fsbo/FsboActions.client.tsx, lib/data/fsbo/dashboard.ts) is dead code with zero importers, including a second unreferenced SMS send path with weaker guards than the live one.

items.requirement: Cron completes within its execution budget across all six service-area cities
items.evidence: lib/fsbo-detector.ts:355-357 calls Apify run-sync-get-dataset-items with `&timeout=180` per city; lib/fsbo-detector.ts:398-411 loops FSBO_SERVICE_AREA_CITIES (6 cities) SEQUENTIALLY (comment at 385-388 says parallelism was deliberately rejected); app/api/cron/detect-fsbo-listings/route.ts:21 sets `maxDuration = 300`. 6 × 180s = 1080s worst case, before lib/fsbo-processor.ts:82-296 runs up to MAX_PER_RUN=15 listings each doing a skip-trace, a CMA queue and a Resend email.
items.gap: Scrape budget exceeds the function budget by up to 3.6x. On any slow Apify day the later cities (Sunriver, Tumalo, La Pine) and the entire per-listing processing loop are silently truncated by the platform — and because each city failure path just returns [] (lib/fsbo-detector.ts:378-381), a partial run is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty market in the response JSON. Fix: cap per-city timeout to ~40s, or move to async actor runs with a follow-up drain cron.
items.why_it_matters: Silent partial coverage means FSBOs in the smaller markets may never be detected at all, and no alarm fires.

items.requirement: Off-market / sold FSBOs are excluded from outreach
items.evidence: The guard exists: lib/data/prospecting/compliance.ts:175 `const offMarket = kind === 'fsbo' ? (prospect.status ?? 'active') !== 'active' : false`, enforced at app/actions/prospecting.ts:123-125. But NOTHING ever writes 'gone': repo-wide grep for a status='gone' write scoped to FSBO returns no matches. The only status writes are lib/fsbo-processor.ts:79 (sets 'active' on re-seen rows) and 289 (sets 'active' on insert). The migration documents the intent at supabase/migrations/20260521161036_fsbo_listings.sql:70 ('active' | 'gone' — last scrape didn't see it) — the reaper was never built.
items.gap: The off-market exclusion is a permanently-false branch. A FSBO that sells, delists, or lists with another brokerage stays status='active' forever and remains sendable in /admin/prospecting indefinitely. This is the single highest-risk defect in the domain: soliciting a property that has since listed with another broker is exactly the conduct the relist guard elsewhere in this file was written to prevent. Fix: after each scrape, mark rows whose last_seen_at is older than the current run (and that were expected in the scraped city set) as status='gone'.
items.why_it_matters: License-risk outreach to owners who are no longer FSBO, and wasted broker time on stale rows.

items.requirement: No dead or duplicate FSBO code paths that can diverge from the live one
items.evidence: app/actions/fsbo-dashboard.ts (208 lines, three server actions) — repo-wide grep shows buildFsboCmaAction imported ONLY by components/admin/fsbo/FsboActions.client.tsx:10, which itself has ZERO importers; sendFsboCmaEmailAction and sendFsboIntroSmsAction have no callers at all. lib/data/fsbo/dashboard.ts is referenced only in comments (lib/data/prospecting/list.ts:6, engagement.ts:8) and is not exported from lib/data/index.ts. All three call revalidatePath('/admin/fsbos') — a route that is now only a redirect.
items.gap: An entire second FSBO outreach stack is sitting in the tree, dead. Critically, the orphaned app/actions/fsbo-dashboard.ts:134-210 sendFsboIntroSmsAction is a WEAKER duplicate of the live sender: it has no claim/idempotency gate, no value-keyed phone suppression, no live relist re-verify, and no pre-send TOCTOU re-check — it guards only on the outreach_sms_sent_at column. If anyone re-wires a button to it (it is a fully working server action, reachable by any client component that imports it), FSBO outreach silently regresses to the pre-hardening posture. Delete all three files.
items.why_it_matters: A live-but-unlinked server action with degraded compliance guards is a loaded gun, not merely clutter.

items.requirement: Multi-source FSBO coverage (Zillow is the only source today)
items.evidence: lib/fsbo-detector.ts:22-27 names FSBO.com, ForSaleByOwner.com, Craigslist and Facebook Marketplace as "Phase 2"; only APIFY_ZILLOW_ACTOR_ID is implemented (line 43). fsbo_source is typed as the literal 'zillow' (lib/fsbo-detector.ts:110), so the type system currently forbids a second source without a change.
items.gap: Single-source dependency on one Apify actor scraping one anti-bot-hardened site. The hardcoded regionId/mapBounds map (lib/fsbo-detector.ts:69-76, captured live 2026-07-14) will silently return zero results whenever Zillow rotates region ids or changes searchQueryState shape — and per the failure path at :378-381 that looks identical to "no FSBOs on the market." There is no zero-result alarm anywhere in the pipeline.
items.why_it_matters: The pipeline can go completely dark without anyone noticing, which is precisely the MV-refresh failure mode this repo has already been burned by.

items.requirement: $500K price floor and SFR-only scoping are correct for FSBO (inherited from the expireds cron)
items.evidence: lib/fsbo-detector.ts:113 FSBO_MIN_LIST_PRICE = 500_000, duplicated into the Zillow query filterState at :92; property-type filter at lib/fsbo-detector.ts:251-254 accepts SFR/Townhouse/Manufactured only. Header comment at :29-34 attributes the floor to "Matt's 2026-05-19 directive" for the EXPIRED cron.
items.gap: Code is internally consistent and tested (lib/fsbo-detector.test.ts:19-22), so this is not a code defect — but the $500K floor was set for expired listings and copied to FSBO without a recorded FSBO-specific decision. FSBO sellers skew toward lower price bands, so the floor may be discarding the bulk of the actual FSBO market. Only Matt can settle whether that is intentional.
items.why_it_matters: If unintentional, the highest-volume slice of the FSBO funnel is being filtered out at the source.

shared_primitives_needed: A scrape-liveness alarm: any detector cron returning zero rows across all geographies for N consecutive runs should page, not log. Both FSBO (lib/fsbo-detector.ts:378-381) and the expireds/Zillow pipelines swallow failures into empty arrays that are indistinguishable from a genuinely empty market.

A generic 'no longer seen in source' reaper for scraped-inventory tables. fsbo_listings.status='gone' is never written; the same last_seen_at staleness pattern applies to expired_listings and any future FSBO source.

A dead-code gate for orphaned server actions. app/actions/fsbo-dashboard.ts is a fully-functional, zero-importer SMS sender with weaker compliance guards than the live path; a CI check for exported server actions with no importers would have caught it (this repo already prefers mechanical gates over prose per CLAUDE.md).
A budget-aware Apify runner: per-call timeouts derived from the route's remaining maxDuration, with partial-run reporting, shared by the FSBO, expired, and competitor-recon crons.

One canonical scraped-prospect schema. fsbo_listings still carries FUB-era column names (fub_person_id, fub_person_matched_by, fub_note_id) that now hold native crm_people ids — a naming trap for every future reader.
open_questions_for_owner: Is the $500,000 price floor intentional for FSBO, or was it copied from the expired-listings directive? FSBO inventory skews lower, so this may be filtering out most of the market.

When a FSBO disappears from the Zillow scrape, should it be marked 'gone' after one missed run, or after N consecutive misses? A single-run rule risks flapping on Apify failures; a multi-run rule leaves a solicitation window open.

Is single-source Zillow coverage acceptable for now, or should Craigslist/FSBO.com be funded as a second source? This is an Apify spend decision, and the $200 usage cap has darkened these pipelines before.

Should the FSBO detection cron run more than once daily? The code comments still assume hourly; the registered schedule is daily at 09:35 UTC. Faster detection means faster first contact but more Apify spend.

Confirm the dead stack (app/actions/fsbo-dashboard.ts, components/admin/fsbo/FsboActions.client.tsx, lib/data/fsbo/dashboard.ts) can be deleted outright rather than kept as a fallback — nothing imports them today.
